text:
Mason Marchment went undrafted, worked his way up through the Marlies, and has now played for six NHL teams. In San Jose this week he made the news for the wrong reason: a $5,000 fine for roughing Islanders rookie Victor Eklund after what he felt was a "pretty dirty" hit, per The Mercury News.

His hockey has been better than his numbers. He's at 16 and a half minutes a night with four goals and seven points in 20 games, and the Sharks have scored 6.4 fewer goals than their chances deserved with him on the ice. That usually swings back. His own chances are about where they should be (four goals on 4.6 expected), and since Igor Chernyshov went down his ice time is up to 18:31. Evolving-Hockey liked him last season, 1.5 wins above replacement, with defence (85th percentile at taking chances away) to go with the scoring. Tonight he needs one goal for 100 in his career, and our range has him at about 19 for the season.
